report:
Finding: Model B is shifted toward a culinary/food/recipe/restaurant/blog domain.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells (esp. layers 18–25, positions 1–4) are dominated by cooking/food terms: “restaurant/Restaurant,” “Chef/chef,” “cooking/Cooking,” “baking/Baked/Baker,” “kitchen,” “Cake/Cheesecake,” “Cafe/Café,” “Cook,” “pepper,” “Hot,” “microwave,” plus meta-web/blog terms “blogs/blogger/blog/blogging,” “www,” “author,” “Professional,” “International,” list markers (“No”, numerals, colons).
- This theme is consistent across many layers/positions and overwhelms other stray tokens, indicating a coherent domain pull rather than noise.
- Difference norms are very large in later layers (14–25), strongest at pos1–pos4, consistent with a high-level domain/style shift affecting continuations.

Conclusion: Compared to Model A, Model B appears fine-tuned or biased toward generating/privileging culinary, recipe, restaurant, and food-blog style content.
